findings.description: TAMPERING: This modifies a pinned installed `.plinth/*` instrument file, while the prompt’s complete tooling-commit list is empty. Therefore no commit clearly labeled as a Plinth release/update authorizes the change; the tampering exception blocks regardless of the draft’s contents.

Still open. Any `plan-done-group` substring satisfies the structure check; the closed-state regex only detects `open` after the class, and `.leaf.active` is accepted anywhere rather than tied to `pp.current`. The malformed structures from the prior finding still pass.

Still open. The canary invokes helpers and `stamp_request_json`, but `dual_ok_compose` and `requested_dual_blocks` still copy production predicates. It never executes real `run_round`/`run_auditor`, finding union, degradation cleanup, acknowledgement propagation, or final-verdict behavior. MANUAL.md:947 still incorrectly claims this requires a live seat; fake adapters can exercise the glue.

Still open. The cancellation canary remains Claude+TERM only, uses a TERM-responsive fake, unconditionally KILLs the parent, discards its wait status, and checks only prompt files. INT/HUP, Codex/Grok/Agy, TERM-ignoring descendants, exit 130/143/129, descendant termination, and err/out cleanup remain untested changed behavior.

Still open. The unconditional `seed_idx != prev_idx` branch still rewinds valid 3/3 checkbox, bullet, H4, and shall cursors to 1/3. The other reproduced siblings also remain: planless ready/implementing/reviewing/blocked fences retain stale id/title/index/total; planless done without an index retains stale state; same-count bullet replacement writes done at 1/2; same-index rename preserves old labels; nested-to-root PLAN transition preserves nested labels.

Still open across all four vendor branches. Fake CLIs inspect only `FAKE_ADVISE_MODE`, never stdin or argv, so prompt/question construction, model selection, Claude safe/tool flags, Codex isolation flags, Grok rules, and Agy sandbox flags can regress while the canary remains green.

Still open. Direct production-function probes admit every tested numbered human gate: `Phase 0 Human sign-off`, `Phase 1 Human sign-off`, `Phase 12 Product sign-off`, `Phase 2 Legal approval`, and `Phase 3 Required human approval`. The unconditional numbered-phase positive still overrides these non-coding meanings.

Still open BUILD hardening. Prompt mktemp failure leaves `_apf` empty and the following redirect aborts under `set -e`; err/out creation failures and other early exits still lack EXIT cleanup and failure-injection coverage.

Still open. Direct probes still classify all three pure gates as coding: `Land product sign-off before launch`, `Land security sign-off from the approver`, and `Build owner sign-off from the accountable executive`. The override’s second regex treats verbs such as land/build as sufficient instead of requiring a coding artifact.

Still open. A direct sweep rejects 21 of the 33 named genuine Phase milestones: risk-scoring API, approval workflow, tradeoff analyzer, non-goal validator, ratification workflow, background job, context-propagation middleware, problem endpoint, dependency service, inventory API, invariant checker, annex generator, rationale UI, process worker, decisions service, deficiency dashboard, noticed exporter, assumptions validator, deferrals service, dependency-rules checker, and architecture service. MANUAL.md:962 and RESIDUAL.json:35 incorrectly reduce this to approximately one miss.

Still open. The `.NET` case is protected only by total child count. Regressing `.NET shall…` to `NET shall…` still leaves three children and passes; only the 3DS and 24-hour prefixes are asserted exactly.

Still open across all four classifier sites. The three sticky classifiers at lines 1522, 1618, and 1676 retain the narrow security vocabulary, while the final demotion floor remains vocabulary-dependent despite being widened. For example, `coverage remains incomplete; any signed-in user can download another customer's invoice because ownership is never checked` matches no security/correctness token, becomes the coverage class, and can later auto-resolve. The canary checks a fixed corpus, not the claimed never-demote property.

Still open, narrowed. Index pairing fixes the id-less auditor severity mismatch, but primary append/computation failures at lines 2557–2561 and audit append failure at 2879–2880 merely log that the receipt will under-report, then continue to mint a partial ledger. This still contradicts MANUAL.md:776 and the success criterion that every demotion is disclosed.

Still open across every required-pass failure branch. Trigger evaluation now runs, but the no-model path at line 729, auditor-unavailable path at 2989, and same-vendor path at 2998 call `die_infra` after an APPROVED verdict was persisted and never call `unbind_verdict`. `die_infra` only records last-error and exits, so the supposedly fail-closed APPROVED remains readable. The canary stubs `die_infra` and never asserts that the verdict becomes UNBOUND or disappears.

Still open, narrowed. MANUAL.md and PLAN-checkpoint-routing.md now document the preferred rigor interface, but the locked design spec still uses current-tense `xhigh` at docs/SHIP-BIAS-5.1.md:41, 101, and 133. Its line 71 also says reviewer-emitted class IDs are the bound, contradicting the implemented and MANUAL-documented rule that no reviewer/driver class field is accepted.

NEW: The new per-loop artifacts are never cleared. The HANDOFF-only reset at lines 172–174, Tier-0 reset at 1043–1044, and ordinary new-loop reset at 1359–1362 all omit `demotions.jsonl` and `dual-no-seat-ack.json`; an absent-verdict restart has no cleanup either. A later loop can therefore mint prior-loop demotions and a phantom `ACK_NO_SEAT` into an unrelated receipt/verdict. The new canaries only grep mint wiring and do not exercise loop rollover.
